note.after_visit_summary: Today we found rough, scaly spots on your scalp that are actinic keratoses, which are precancerous spots from sun exposure. We also saw harmless, waxy spots on your back called seborrheic keratoses. The spot on your left cheek where a skin cancer was removed in 2021 looks healed and fine. We treated the 6 spots on your scalp with liquid nitrogen freezing. Over the next few days, they may get red, blister, or crust, and should peel off in 1 to 3 weeks. You can use petroleum jelly on them if they feel uncomfortable. If any spot does not heal in 6 weeks or starts to grow, come back so we can check it further. To prevent more spots, use a broad-spectrum sunscreen with SPF 30 or higher every morning on your scalp, face, ears, and hands. Reapply every 2 hours when you are outside. Wear a wide-brimmed hat that covers your ears and neck instead of your seed cap, and consider long sleeves for added protection. We want to see you back in 6 months for a full skin check because of your history of skin cancer. Put this follow-up visit on your calendar after harvest.
